newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo accepts all IMF membership terms - Tanjug.
newsitem.headline: Yugo accepts all IMF membership terms - Tanjug.

text.p: Yugoslavia told the International Monetary Fund (IMF) that it accepted the IMF membership terms set in 1992, Tanjug news agency reported on Wednesday.

"The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (FRY), in accordance with its laws, accepts the membership in the fund and participation in the special drawing rights under conditions and terms set by the decision of the IMF Board of Directors on December 14, 1992," the agency quoted the government report.

"FRY accepts its quota of the assets and liabilities of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to be as determined in paragraph 2(a) of the decision," the report said quoting a letter from federal Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to Michael Camdessus, the IMF director.

Last August, parliament endorsed the government decision to accept a quota of 36.52 percent of the assets and liabilities of the former Yugoslav federation in the Fund. It also agreed to pay back its outstanding debt of $104 million.
Yugoslavia has to decide by December 14 if it wants its status in the IMF to be resolved or ask for another six month postponement.

Analysts said on Tuesday that the way the Yugoslav authorities were handling opposition protests over alleged election fraud would delay a return to the Fund. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
